sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Lesson 3.2, Kaito! Today we tackle the five global pillars of AI ethics: Non-Maleficence, Fairness, Transparency, Accountability, and Respect for Autonomy.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Honestly, Dr. Nova, I see those five words framed on office posters everywhere, yet models still fail minority patients and lock consumers out of loans. Why don't mission statements prevent harm?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Because in production machine learning, an ethical principle without a deterministic assertion in your CI/CD pipeline is merely decorative! Each principle must compile down to mathematical disparity bounds, proxy audits, and executable release blockers.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Love that! Let's break down the exact math and case studies that turn moral philosophy into strict software engineering contracts.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at Row 5 of Table 3.1: Autonomy isn't just a privacy policy link—you actually test for granular opt-in toggles and automated deletion DAGs across data lakes?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Absolutely, Kaito! Dynamic Informed Consent Registries let patients grant oncology access while disallowing ad modeling via signed API tokens. Meanwhile, pre-ticked checkboxes or forced service bundling violate GDPR Article 7(4) and render the entire training corpus legally toxic.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: And similarly, Non-Maleficence checks worst-case subgroup risk sup R sub g, Fairness enforces Disparate Impact Ratio at least 0.80, Transparency demands SHAP explanations, and Accountability requires cryptographic provenance!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, most machine learning training loops minimize mean population cross-entropy—isn't that basically Utilitarian Aggregate Welfare?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Exactly! Standard empirical risk minimization acts like pure utilitarianism. If a hospital dataset is 90 percent majority patients and 10 percent minority patients, minimizing average loss achieves a stellar aggregate metric even if it ignores the minority completely!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So Rawlsian Maximin flips the objective to optimize the minimum subgroup utility across all protected cohorts, while the Benefit-to-Risk Ratio explicitly penalizes high variance in catastrophic harms!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, why do we need three separate equations for fairness? Doesn't passing the EEOC Four-Fifths Rule on Disparate Impact Ratio automatically guarantee fairness?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not at all, Kaito! Demographic Parity only checks overall acceptance rates without checking who actually deserves approval. You could satisfy DIR equals 1.0 by accepting qualified Group A applicants and randomly selecting unqualified Group B applicants!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Aha! That's why Equalized Odds conditions on the true outcome Y—matching False Positive and True Positive rates across cohorts—while Predictive Parity checks whether risk scores mean the same calibration probability regardless of group!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Wait, Dr. Nova—you mean even the best engineering team on Earth literally cannot satisfy Demographic Parity, Equalized Odds, and Predictive Parity at the exact same time?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Unless your model makes zero errors—100% True Positive Rate and 0% False Positive Rate—it is mathematically impossible whenever base prevalence differs between groups! Look at Bayes' equation: PPV depends on the product of base odds and the FPR-to-TPR ratio.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So teams must explicitly choose and document which fairness definition fits their clinical or legal context—and pair predictions with Shapley feature attributions so users know why a decision occurred!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, I loaded the exact 1,000-patient Obermeyer simulation right below. Look at Preset 1 using Historical Healthcare Cost as the target label.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Whoa! Utilitarian welfare says 0.88, which looks totally deployable—until you glance at Group B Clinical Recall and the Rawlsian Maximin floor! Let's dock at the simulator and toggle to Preset 3 Biomarker Grounding!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: The hospital procurement contract literally requires BOTH identical FPR/TPR across ages AND identical PPV calibration—with 12 percent elderly sepsis prevalence versus 3 percent for young adults!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Check Bayes' formula for PPV! Test your mastery in Checkpoint 1 below by choosing Option A, B, or C!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Wait, Dr. Nova—did the healthcare engineers even include race as an input feature in that 200-million-patient triage algorithm?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: No! Race wasn't even a feature! The bias came entirely from label choice: setting y equal to historical healthcare dollars spent instead of actual biological illness. When Black patients face barriers to hospital utilization, spending drops even when hypertension and renal disease are worse.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: And simply redefining the target label around real lab biomarkers like HbA1c boosted qualified Black patient enrollment by 84 percent!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at the COMPAS dispute between ProPublica and Northpointe: Northpointe insisted their tool was fair because 'High Risk' meant a 60 percent re-arrest probability for both races, while ProPublica called it deeply biased!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Mathematically, both sides were measuring real properties! Northpointe enforced Predictive Parity calibration, whereas ProPublica exposed a massive Equalized Odds failure—44.9 percent false positives for Black defendants versus 23.5 percent for white defendants!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: And in Amazon's hiring tool, simply deleting the word 'women' couldn't erase 10 years of male-skewed history because neural embeddings latched onto latent proxies instead!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at our fintech credit underwriting scenario: the engineers stripped race, ethnicity, and ZIP code from the feature store, yet an audit still measured Disparate Impact Ratio at 0.58! How is that possible?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Because of Redundant Feature Encoding! High-capacity models like XGBoost effortlessly combine subtle correlates—high school graduation year, smartphone OS, merchant category codes, and payment timestamps—whenever mutual information I of X and G exceeds zero!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So removing protected attributes actually blinds our own auditors without stopping the model! Instead, we need adversarial debiasing, counterfactual data augmentation, and SHAP adverse action notices that offer genuine recourse.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, if a human judge signs off on every bail risk recommendation and our database engineering team deletes revoked user rows from Postgres, aren't Accountability and Autonomy both covered?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Neither is covered, Kaito! Under cognitive overload, judges rubber-stamp 98.4 percent of automated outputs—creating a moral crumple zone without meaningful oversight. And deleting row r sub i from Postgres leaves its gradient updates permanently baked inside neural weights!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So true Accountability demands documented human friction and peer audits, while true Autonomy requires SISA sharded machine unlearning!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, dock down to the Chouldechova Fairness Trilemma Workbench and set Group 0 prevalence to 12 percent and Group 1 prevalence to 3 percent—just like our ICU sepsis case.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Whoa! Under Equalized Odds, calibration PPV jumps by more than 25 percentage points between cohorts! And switching to Predictive Parity immediately forces a huge FPR gap! Try adjusting the sliders right below!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Wait—dropping race and ZIP code, adding a 98.4% rubber-stamp human reviewer, AND deleting revoked rows from SQL all sound reasonable on paper, yet all three fail ethical audits!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let's test whether our engineers can pinpoint all three technical traps in Checkpoint 2 below—select Option A, B, or C!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: I love how concrete these remedies are: counterfactual augmentation and subgroup error regularization instead of naive blinding; mandatory justification friction instead of rubber-stamping; and Dynamic Consent plus SISA instead of dark patterns.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Exactly, Kaito! Next, let's inspect the actual production Python gatekeeper that turns Rawlsian Maximin, Disparate Impact Ratio, and Equalized Odds into an automated CI/CD blocker.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at that conjunction inside is_deployable: rawlsian >= 0.70 AND dir_ratio >= 0.80 AND eq_odds <= 0.15! Even if utilitarian average welfare is 0.90, failing ANY single subgroup threshold fails the build!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: That is exactly how ethical principles become non-negotiable engineering contracts! In test_ethical_audit_assertions, depressing minority predictions drops rawlsian_maximin_welfare below 0.60 and triggers an immediate CI/CD gate failure.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: What an eye-opening deep dive, Dr. Nova! Seeing how Obermeyer's healthcare cost proxy harmed Black patients by 84 percent, why COMPAS proved Chouldechova's Impossibility Theorem live, and how Pydantic V2 gates enforce Rawlsian floors completely changed how I view fairness.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Always remember: never trust aggregate accuracy alone, never rely on Fairness Through Blindness, and always turn ethical values into executable code assertions! Next up in Lesson 3.3, we explore Utility Dilemmas and Consequences. See you there!
